extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and agencies, agency rulewriters, and regulatory reviewers (federal regulatory officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and procedural requirements for federal agencies to follow when developing, reviewing, and revising regulations, including standards for analysis, public participation, science, flexibility, and retrospective review.  Targets agency decisionmaking and submission of plans to OIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect public health, welfare, safety, and environment while promoting economic growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Our regulatory system must protect public health, welfare, safety, and our environment while promoting economic growth, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations should balance protection goals with promotion of economic objectives such as innovation and jobs; this is a foundational objective for rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base regulations on the best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory system must be based on the best available science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific and technical evidence used to support regulatory actions should reflect current, reliable science; see also requirement to ensure objectivity in Section 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow public participation and open exchange of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must allow for public participation and an open exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking processes should be structured to enable input from stakeholders, experts, and the public (expanded in Section 2 with specific online and comment-period requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote predictability and reduce uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory system must promote predictability and reduce uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule design and implementation should favor clarity and stability where feasible so regulated parties can plan and comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the best, most innovative, and least burdensome tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory system must identify and use the best, most innovative, and least burdensome tools for achieving regulatory ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider alternative tools (including non‑regulatory ones) and choose approaches that achieve objectives while minimizing burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take into account benefits and costs, both quantitative and qualitative
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory decisions must take into account benefits and costs, both quantitative and qualitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider a broad set of effects in regulatory analysis, not only easily quantified monetary impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure regulations are accessible, consistent, plain language, and easy to understand
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must be accessible, consistent, written in plain language, and easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting should prioritize clarity and consistency across rules to improve compliance and reduce uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and seek to improve actual results of regulatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory programs must measure, and seek to improve, the actual results of regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should track outcomes and use empirical evidence to refine regulations and improve effectiveness over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose/adopt regulation only upon reasoned determination that benefits justify costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must propose or adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that its benefits justify its costs (recognizing that some benefits and costs are difficult to quantify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory decisions should be supported by reasoned analysis demonstrating net benefits or other justification; when quantification is difficult, qualitative discussion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor regulations to impose the least burden consistent with objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor regulations to impose the least burden on society, consistent with obtaining regulatory objectives, taking into account, among other things, and to the extent practicable, the costs of cumulative regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternatives and design rules that minimize economic and administrative burdens, including interaction with other regulations (cumulative costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select approaches that maximize net benefits, including distributive impacts and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: In choosing among alternative regulatory approaches, select those approaches that maximize net benefits (including potential economic, environmental, public health and safety, and other advantages; distributive impacts; and equity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should weigh multiple dimensions of benefit and harm, and explicitly consider distributional consequences and equity where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify performance objectives rather than prescriptive behavior when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent feasible, specify performance objectives, rather than specifying the behavior or manner of compliance that regulated entities must adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for performance-based standards that allow flexibility in how regulated parties achieve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and assess alternatives to direct regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and assess available alternatives to direct regulation, including providing economic incentives to encourage the desired behavior, such as user fees or marketable permits, or providing information upon which choices can be made by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider non‑regulatory or market-based approaches and information-based interventions as means to achieve regulatory goals with lower burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best available techniques to quantify anticipated present and future benefits and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency is directed to use the best available techniques to quantify anticipated present and future benefits and costs as accurately as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply state‑of‑the‑art analytic methods and transparent assumptions in cost‑benefit estimation; when quantification is infeasible, discuss qualitative values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and discuss values difficult to quantify (equity, dignity, fairness, distributive impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate and permitted by law, each agency may consider (and discuss qualitatively) values that are difficult or impossible to quantify, including equity, human dignity, fairness, and distributive impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should acknowledge and qualitatively analyze important non‑monetary values alongside quantified estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt regulations through a process involving broad public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall be adopted through a process that involves public participation. To that end, regulations shall be based, to the extent feasible and consistent with law, on the open exchange of information and perspectives among State, local, and tribal officials, experts in relevant disciplines, affected stakeholders in the private sector, and the public as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage outreach and engagement across levels of government, disciplines, and stakeholder groups when developing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide meaningful Internet-based opportunity to comment (generally at least 60 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall afford the public a meaningful opportunity to comment through the Internet on any proposed regulation, with a comment period that should generally be at least 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default expectation is a 60‑day public comment period via online submission unless law or circumstances justify otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely online access to rulemaking docket and scientific/technical findings in open, searchable format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide, for both proposed and final rules, timely online access to the rulemaking docket on regulations.gov, including relevant scientific and technical findings, in an open format that can be easily searched and downloaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dockets should be complete, accessible, and machine‑readable when feasible to enable informed public review and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow public comment on all pertinent parts of the rulemaking docket for proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed rules, such access shall include, to the extent feasible and permitted by law, an opportunity for public comment on all pertinent parts of the rulemaking docket, including relevant scientific and technical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that documents and evidence underlying proposals are made available in time for meaningful public comment on those materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek views of those likely to be affected before issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, each agency, where feasible and appropriate, shall seek the views of those who are likely to be affected, including those who are likely to benefit from and those who are potentially subject to such rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders early (pre‑NPR outreach) to identify concerns, alternatives, and informational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote coordination, simplification, and harmonization across agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing regulatory actions and identifying appropriate approaches, each agency shall attempt to promote such coordination, simplification, and harmonization [to reduce redundant, inconsistent, or overlapping requirements].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple agencies regulate similar subjects, seek cross‑agency solutions to reduce duplication and conflicting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify approaches to achieve regulatory goals that promote innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall also seek to identify, as appropriate, means to achieve regulatory goals that are designed to promote innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider regulatory designs that encourage technological or business model innovation while meeting policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider flexible regulatory approaches that reduce burdens and preserve choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, feasible, and consistent with regulatory objectives, and to the extent permitted by law, each agency shall identify and consider regulatory approaches that reduce burdens and maintain flexibility and freedom of choice for the public. These approaches include warnings, appropriate default rules, and disclosure requirements as well as provision of information to the public in a form that is clear and intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize less intrusive interventions (warnings, defaults, disclosures, information) when they can achieve policy goals effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure objectivity of scientific and technological information and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall ensure the objectivity of any scientific and technological information and processes used to support the agency's regulatory actions (consistent with the President's Memorandum 'Scientific Integrity' and its implementing guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and follow scientific integrity practices to prevent bias and maintain credibility of the evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct retrospective analysis of existing significant regulations and release supporting data online
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall consider how best to promote retrospective analysis of rules that may be outmoded, ineffective, insufficient, or excessively burdensome, and to modify, streamline, expand, or repeal them in accordance with what has been learned. Such retrospective analyses, including supporting data, should be released online whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical review to identify regulations for reform; publish analyses and data to enable transparency and public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit preliminary plan to OIRA within 120 days for periodic review of significant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of the date of this order, each agency shall develop and submit to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs a preliminary plan, consistent with law and its resources and regulatory priorities, under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any such regulations should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed so as to make the agency's regulatory program more effective or less burdensome in achieving the regulatory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prepare and send a practicable plan to OIRA outlining how they will perform periodic retrospective reviews of significant rules.
